title: The Khalsa Crosses the Rivers to Fight for the Brahmin

blocks.text: The Khalsa accepts the appeal and pushes eastward despite the risks of operating near Delhi's orbit. After crossing the Satluj they camp near the bank of the river Yamuna, and news of their approach sends the local Muslim authorities into hurried defensive preparation.

The advance then becomes personal and symbolic at once. With the (aggrieved) Brahmin leading them from the front, the Singhs cross onward, raise their standards, and pray that they may win martyrdom while carrying out an act of welfare for others.

Their charge immediately shakes the defenders. The enemy falls back toward the gates under pressure, and the page presents the coming assault as righteous intervention rather than opportunistic raiding.
